quickExit.label: Quick exit
quickExit.hint: Leaves this site immediately and clears this page. Shortcut: Shift + Esc.

display.title: Display and reading
display.wideLettersHint: Can make reading easier, for example with dyslexia
display.colours: Colours: light, dark or eye care
display.discreetHint: The browser tab shows "Notes" instead of SpeakSafe

readAloud.noUrdu: This device has no Urdu voice installed. You can add one in your phone or computer's speech settings.

idle.title: Are you still there?
idle.body: To protect your privacy, your space will lock in about a minute. Anything you saved stays safe.

home.title: A safe place to speak up.
home.intro: Take your time. Nothing is shared until you choose.

privacy.title: Your privacy
privacy.p1: No email, phone or real name needed
privacy.p2: Your IP address is not stored
privacy.p3: Everything is encrypted on your device

how.title: How SpeakSafe works
how.s1b: A made-up username and a password. No email or real name.
how.s2b: Keep a private journal and evidence. Nothing is shared.
how.s3b: Choose who can read it, and whether they know who you are.

help.title: Need help now?
help.body: If you are in danger, call:

err.username: Use 3 to 32 lower-case letters or numbers, with single hyphens between them.
err.passwordWeak: This password is easy to guess. Try three or more random words.
err.mismatch: The two passwords are not the same.

signup.title: Create your private space
signup.intro: One place for your journal, reports and messages. Only you can open it.
signup.usernameHint: We made one up for you. Please don't use your real name.
signup.passwordHint: Tip: three or more random words are easy to remember and hard to guess.
signup.privacyNote: No email, no phone number, no real name. Even if you report as Anonymous, the committee never sees your username.
signup.wordsIntro: If you forget your password, these 6 words are the only way back in.
signup.wordsWarning: Write them on paper and keep them somewhere safe. Nobody can recover them for you, not even us. That is what keeps your space private.
signup.checkTitle: Quick check: type word {{a}} and word {{b}}
signup.checkHint: Type the two words above to continue.

login.title: Welcome back
login.intro: Log in to your private space.
login.missing: Please enter your username and password.
login.forgot: Forgot your password? Use your recovery words
login.sharedNote: On a shared device? Your space locks itself after 10 minutes without activity.
login.staffHint: This is the login for reporters. Committee members sign in on the Committee login page (link below).

recover.title: Use your recovery words
recover.intro: Type your username and your 6 recovery words, then choose a new password.
recover.wordsHint: Tip: paste all six words into the first box.
recover.badWord: Word {{n}} isn't one of the recovery words we use. Please check the spelling.

space.title: You're doing the right thing by being here.
space.welcomeNew: Your private space is ready. Keep your recovery words safe.
space.recovered: Your new password is set. You were logged out everywhere else.
space.sub: Take things one step at a time. You can stop and come back whenever you like.
space.safe1: Only your password can unlock what you save here.
space.safe2: The committee never sees your username.
space.safe3: Keep your 6 recovery words somewhere safe.

break.title: Take a moment
break.intro: There's no rush. Breathe with the circle.
break.pattern: In for 4 · hold for 4 · out for 6
break.talk: Talk to someone: support and helplines

placeholder.soon: This section is coming in the next build step.

errors.network: We can't reach SpeakSafe right now. Please check your internet connection and try again.
errors.generic: Something went wrong. Please try again.

authShell.title: Your story stays yours.
authShell.body: SpeakSafe locks everything on your own device before it is sent. Only the people you choose can read your report.
authShell.foot: Free and confidential. Leave any time with Quick exit.

q.3: Do you have anything that shows what happened?
q.4: How would you like to be known?
q.5: Is there anyone who should NOT see this?

help.1: Choose the closest one. You can change it later.
help.2: Use your own words. Leave out anything you are not sure about.
help.3: Photos, screenshots or documents. This step is optional.
help.4: This only changes what the committee knows about you. Your report is protected the same way in every option.
help.5: If a committee member is involved or close to the person, keep them away. They will never be able to open your report.
help.6: Nothing is sent until you press Send.

need.1: Please choose the type of concern to continue.
need.2: Please describe what happened, in writing or as a voice note.
need.4: Please choose an option. For Confidential or Named, please add your name.
need.5: At least two committee members must be able to read your report.

report.howTell: How do you want to tell us?
report.descOptional: Anything you'd like to add in writing (optional)
report.descPlaceholder: Start anywhere. A few sentences is enough.
report.whereHint: For example: a building, a class or an online group. Leave it out if it could identify you.
report.contactHint: An email or phone number. Only the assigned members will see it.
report.startOver: Discard this draft and start over

save.error: Couldn't save just now. We'll try again.

evidence.cleanNote: Hidden details like location, the date a photo was taken and the phone model are removed from every file on your device, before anything is sent.
evidence.limits: Up to {{n}} files, 10 MB each. Photos (JPG, PNG, WebP) and PDFs.
evidence.badType: That type of file can't be added. Please use a photo (JPG, PNG, WebP) or a PDF.
evidence.tooBig: That file is larger than 10 MB.
evidence.cantRead: We couldn't read that file. If it's a password-protected PDF, please remove the password first.

ANONYMOUS.title: Anonymous
ANONYMOUS.body: The committee won't know who you are.
ANONYMOUS.limits: Even without your name, small details (like an exact day, place, or how few people were there) could make it possible to guess who you are. You can leave those out or keep them general.

CONFIDENTIAL.title: Confidential
CONFIDENTIAL.body: Only your assigned committee members see your name and contact.
CONFIDENTIAL.who: Only the two assigned members can see this. It is locked inside your report.

NAMED.title: Named
NAMED.body: Your name is part of the report.
NAMED.who: Your name will be part of the report the committee reads.

exclude.tooMany: At least two committee members must be able to read your report. Please untick someone.
exclude.note: Your report will be locked for two of the members you didn't tick.

review.lockNote: When you press Send, your report and files are locked on this device so that only the two assigned committee members can open them.

voice.unsupported: This browser can't record audio. You can type instead, or try Chrome or Edge.
voice.denied: We couldn't use the microphone. Please allow microphone access in your browser, then try again.
voice.limit: Up to 5 minutes. You can pause.
voice.stopHint: Press the square to save your voice note.
voice.locked: Locked on this device before it is sent

dictation.unsupported: Dictation isn't available in this browser. Try a voice note instead.
dictation.consentBody: To turn speech into text, your browser may send your voice to Google or Microsoft. For the most privacy, record a voice note instead: it is locked on your device.
dictation.appendHint: Your words appear in the box below, where you can correct them.

sent.title: Your report has been sent.
sent.body: That took courage. You don't have to do anything else right now.
sent.failed_one: Your report was sent, but {{count}} file could not be added. You can add it later from your case.
sent.failed_other: Your report was sent, but {{count}} files could not be added. You can add them later from your case.
sent.fingerprintHint: A unique code made from your locked report. If anyone changed even one letter, this seal would no longer match.
sent.next1: Two committee members can now read your report. Usually they look at it within 2 working days.
sent.next2: You'll see updates under My cases whenever you log in.

cases.title: My cases
cases.intro: Only you can see this list.
cases.empty: You haven't sent a report yet.
cases.emptyHint: When you do, it will appear here with its progress and any messages.

caseView.notFound: We couldn't find this case in your private space.

statusLine.RECEIVED: Your report has arrived. The committee will look at it soon.
statusLine.UNDER_REVIEW: Your case is being looked at.
statusLine.INQUIRY: A formal inquiry is taking place.
statusLine.PENDING_CLOSURE: The committee is getting ready to close this case.

caseView.onlyReaders: Only you and the assigned members
caseView.messagesSoon: No messages yet. When the committee writes to you, it will appear here. You can also write to them.
caseView.addMoreHint: Remembered something, or found more evidence? Add photos or PDFs. Hidden details are removed first.

messages.locked: Encrypted · only you and the assigned members
messages.placeholder: Write a message… (Ctrl + Enter to send)
messages.closed: This case is closed, so new messages can't be sent.

journal.title: Your journal
journal.sub: Write things down while they are fresh. Short notes are enough. You can decide later whether to report.
journal.private: Only you can read this. Your journal and files are locked with your password before they leave this device. The committee never sees them unless you add them to a report.
journal.chooseHelp: Tick the entries and files you want to add to a report. Files attached to an entry come along with it. Nothing is sent until you review the report and press Send.
journal.addedToReport: Added from your journal: {{entries}} entries and {{files}} files. Please check the description and files, then continue.
journal.tooManyFiles: That is more than 10 photos and documents for one report. Please choose fewer files.
journal.tooManyVoice: A report can hold 2 voice notes. Please choose fewer voice notes.
journal.emptyBody: Your first entry can be just a few words. Dates can be rough, and you can add a voice note instead of typing.
journal.lockerEmptyBody: Keep screenshots, photos and documents here. Hidden details are removed from each file before it is stored.
journal.whatPlaceholder: Write as much or as little as you like…
journal.whatHint: Who was there, what was said, how you felt. Anything that helps you remember.
journal.filesNote: Files you add here are also kept in your evidence locker.
journal.needSomething: Please write something or add a voice note or file first.
journal.confirmEntry: Delete this entry? This cannot be undone.
journal.confirmEntryFiles: Delete this entry? Its files stay in your evidence locker.
journal.confirmFile: Delete this file? This cannot be undone.
journal.confirmFileUsed_one: Delete this file? It will also be removed from {{count}} entry.
journal.confirmFileUsed_other: Delete this file? It will also be removed from {{count}} entries.

options.title: Know your options
options.sub: Short answers to the questions most people have before reporting. Take your time; you don't have to decide anything today.

counts.title: Does what happened count?
counts.body: If something made you feel unsafe, treated unfairly or worried, it is worth writing down. You don't need to be sure it "counts" or have proof. The committee can help work that out.

ex.Harassment: Unwanted comments, messages, touching, following, or pressure, in person or online.
ex.Discrimination: Being treated worse because of gender, religion, disability, background or similar.
ex.Academic misconduct: Cheating, plagiarism, grades in exchange for favours, unfair marking.
ex.Fraud or financial misconduct: Misuse of money or funds, bribes, fake documents.
ex.Safety concern: Something that could hurt people: unsafe buildings, threats, violence.
ex.Other: Anything else that worries you. Describe it in your own words.

counts.unsure: Not sure? Write it in your journal first. You can decide later.

next.title: What happens after you report?
next.body: You can follow every step from My cases. You will see when your report is first opened, and each change of status.

received.b: Your report is stored, locked, with its tamper-proof seal. Two committee members are chosen to read it.

read.b: Only those two members can unlock it. You see the date it was first opened.

review.b: They look at what you shared. They may send you questions in My cases; you choose what to answer.

inquiry.b: If needed, the committee looks into it further under your institution's rules.

closure.b: Closing needs two members to agree. Your report and all messages are kept; nothing can be deleted.

next.note: SpeakSafe does not send emails or texts. New messages show as a badge when you log in.

modes.title: Anonymous, confidential or named?
modes.body: You choose this for each report. The content is encrypted in every case; this choice is only about whether the committee knows who you are.

ANONYMOUS.name: Nobody. The committee never sees your username either.
ANONYMOUS.good: You fear retaliation, or just want the problem known.

CONFIDENTIAL.name: Only the two members reading your report.
CONFIDENTIAL.good: You want help that may need your identity, without others knowing.

NAMED.name: Your name is part of the report.
NAMED.good: You want formal action and are comfortable being known.

modes.change: You can still message the committee in all three options. A report cannot be changed after sending, but you can add information later.

who.title: Who can read your report?
who.body: Your report is locked on your device before it is sent. Only people who hold a key can unlock it.

can.members: The two committee members chosen for your case (another member only if one steps aside).

cannot.excluded: Any member you chose to keep away.
cannot.server: The server or database: they only store locked data.

who.log: Every time a member opens your case, it is recorded in a log that cannot be changed, and you see the date.

limits.title: What SpeakSafe cannot promise
limits.body: We tell you this honestly so you can decide what to share.
limits.style: Your way of writing, or details only you would know, could hint at who you are. Keep details general if you want to stay anonymous.
limits.small: In a very small group (for example one class of 10), people may guess who reported, even without a name.
limits.device: Someone with access to your phone or laptop could see that you use SpeakSafe. Use Quick Exit, the discreet tab name, and log out when you finish.
limits.words: If you forget your password and lose your 6 recovery words, nobody can open your private space, not even us.

choices.title: Your choices
choices.body: There is no wrong choice. You can also do more than one.

wait.b: You don't have to act now. Your private space stays here.

journal.b: Write down dates and details and keep evidence in your locker, just for you.

talk.b: A helpline or a person you trust can listen and advise. See Support.

report.b: Anonymously, confidentially or by name, and choose who must not see it.

outside.b: For example to the Federal Ombudsperson for workplace harassment, or to the police. See Support.

support.title: Support and helplines
support.sub: People and services who can listen, advise or act. Choose a type of concern to see who can help.
support.privacy: Calls and emails go from your own phone or email, outside SpeakSafe, and may appear in your call log or browser history. Websites open in a new tab.
support.checked: Numbers last checked: {{date}}. Services sometimes change their numbers.

emergency.name: Emergency: Police 15 · Rescue 1122
emergency.what: If you or someone else is in danger right now, call immediately.

campus.name: Your university's harassment committee
campus.by: Required at every university by the HEC policy on protection against sexual harassment (2020)
campus.what: Every university must have an inquiry committee. Your student affairs office can tell you who is on it. You can also report to them through SpeakSafe.

fospah.name: Federal Ombudsperson for Protection Against Harassment (FOSPAH)
fospah.what: Takes complaints about harassment at the workplace, including universities, and can order action.

pcsw.name: Women's helpline 1043 (Punjab)
pcsw.by: Punjab Commission on the Status of Women
pcsw.what: Free advice on workplace harassment, discrimination and violence, with legal advisors and a counsellor.

sindh.name: Women's helpline 1094 (Sindh)
sindh.by: Women Development Department, Government of Sindh
sindh.what: Information, guidance and support for women facing violence or harassment.

drf.name: Cyber Harassment Helpline
drf.what: Free, confidential help with online harassment, blackmail, fake accounts and leaked pictures.

humanRights.name: Human rights helpline 1099
humanRights.what: Free legal advice on human rights violations, including discrimination and violence.

madadgaar.name: Madadgaar National Helpline 1098
madadgaar.by: Lawyers for Human Rights and Legal Aid (LHRLA)
madadgaar.what: Help for children and women facing abuse or violence.
